## 1. FOR-GEM-03 · Forge: the function spec, written as the build plan

**Due:** 2026-11-24 · **State:** delivered 2026-11-16, waiting for its check: do not redo it unless a review reopens it

**Why:** Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.

**What it unlocks:** Joseph goes pillar by pillar, function before form; this file is the plan Claude builds Forge from, step by step.

**Read first:**
- https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/forge/
- https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/pillars/forge
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/docs/CHARTER.md (section 16: protections)

**Do this:**
1. Open the live page (https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/forge/) on a phone-sized browser and use every section.
2. Read the code (https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/pillars/forge): every file the page loads, and pillar.json.
3. Write section A from what is there now, with file:line for each item; then B to H.
4. Write for Claude to build from: exact, testable, nothing vague like 'improve the UX'.

**Make:** `forge_gemini_function-spec_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.md`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `one markdown file with exactly these headings, in this order: A What it does today | B What Joseph needs it to do | C Data | D Screens | E Rules and edge cases | F Acceptance tests | G Order of work | H Must not`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `A What it does today` (list): every section, control and number on the live page, each with the file and line in the code that makes it (e.g. app.js:142)
- `B What Joseph needs it to do` (8+ user stories): 'As Joseph, when ..., I want ..., so that ...'; from the pillar's mission and its own data; never invent facts about his life
- `C Data` (table): record | field | type | unit | required | example | storage key (prometheus.<pillar>.<name>) | read by which other pillar
- `D Screens` (per screen): purpose; every element top to bottom; every number with its formula and source field; the empty state text; the error state
- `E Rules and edge cases` (10+): dates and time zones, missing data, offline, two devices, a value of 0 vs unknown
- `F Acceptance tests` (12+): Given / When / Then, each checkable in a phone browser in under two minutes
- `G Order of work` (numbered steps): each step small enough for one build, with what Joseph can use after it
- `H Must not` (list): the charter's protections that apply, no server or account, no made-up numbers

**One finished row, as an example (use your own data, never copy this):**

```
F7. Given an oil change logged at 12,000 mi and a 6,000 mi interval, when the odometer is set to 17,500 mi, then the service card shows 'due in 500 mi' in amber.
```

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every item in A has a file:line that exists.
- [ ] B has 8+ stories and none invents a personal fact.
- [ ] C names every field with type and example.
- [ ] F has 12+ tests, each with one Given, one When, one Then.
- [ ] G steps are in an order that can ship one by one.
- [ ] All eight headings, in order.

**How many:** 1

**Done when:** 1 file exactly in the shape, every self-check line true.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude opens 10 rows (or 10 claims) at random and compares them with their source.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field
- a row copied from another row with the names changed
- a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
- a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
- a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
- a guess written as a fact (say 'not found' instead)
- anything about Joseph's own accounts, balances, mail or records beyond what the task names

## 2. FOR-GEM-04 · Forge: a checker that tells an AI (and Claude) whether a homework file matches its task before it is saved

**Due:** 2026-11-28 · **State:** now

**Why:** Most rejected deliveries fail on things a script can see: wrong name, wrong count, a missing field, a home-page URL, a duplicate row. Today Claude finds them by hand after the fact.

**What it unlocks:** Every AI can run one command on its file before saving, and the Forge can mark a delivery 'shape OK' the moment it lands.

**Read first:**
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/docs/agents/queues.json and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/garage/docs/agents/queues.json (the task shape: deliver.file, count, fields)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/proofs/unit/ (how the unit proofs are written: node --test)

**Do this:**
1. Write tools/kit/check_delivery.mjs (Node 20, no dependencies). Usage: node tools/kit/check_delivery.mjs <file> [<task id>]. With no id, find the task whose deliver.file pattern matches the file name ({YYYYMMDD-HHMM} = 8 digits, dash, 4 digits) across docs/agents/queues.json and pillars/*/docs/agents/queues.json.
2. Checks, each printed as PASS or FAIL with the reason: (1) the file name matches the pattern; (2) a .json file parses; (3) the array length equals count when count > 0; (4) every object has exactly the field names in fields, no more, no fewer; (5) type checks: integer, number, date (YYYY-MM-DD), URL (https, has a path other than '/', not a search page: no 'search', 'q=' or 's=' query); (6) no two rows are equal after lower-casing and trimming every text field except n; (7) any field named quote is 300 characters or fewer; (8) for .md files, every heading the task's shape names is present. Exit code 1 if any check fails.
3. Write proofs/unit/check-delivery.test.mjs with 12 cases (6 that pass, 6 that each fail one named check) and their fixture files under proofs/fixtures/check-delivery/. Run node --test yourself and paste the output into a comment at the top of the test file.

**Make:** `forge_gemini_check-delivery_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.zip (or the three paths as separate files with the same stamp)`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `tools/kit/check_delivery.mjs, proofs/unit/check-delivery.test.mjs, proofs/fixtures/check-delivery/*`

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] node --test proofs/unit/check-delivery.test.mjs passes on a clean checkout of the repo with your files added.
- [ ] The script has no dependencies and reads only the repo and the given file.
- [ ] Running it on garage_gemini_specs (any real delivery) gives a sensible result.

**How many:** 12

**Done when:** Claude adds the files to a checkout and node --test passes 12 of 12, and the checker gives the right verdict on 3 real deliveries from Drive.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude runs the tests and the script on 3 real deliveries.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- a test that passes because it checks nothing
- a dependency or network call
- fewer than 12 cases
- files saved anywhere but the folder named here
